extracted.intended_audience: EPO examiners and formalities officers; patent attorneys and applicants interacting with the EPO as RO/(S)ISA/IPEA under the PCT
extracted.subtask_description: Official EPO Guidelines for search and examination when the EPO acts as a PCT Authority (RO, (S)ISA, IPEA). Covers formalities, fees, search practice, unity, patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial application), amendments, corrections and related procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part G deals with excluded subject-matter (Art.17(2)(a)(i) and Rule 39; Art.34(4)(a)(i) and Rule 67), novelty (Art.33(2)), inventive step (Art.33(3)) and industrial application (Art.33(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where practice for EP and PCT is the same (e.g. assessment of novelty), cross‑references to the EP Guidelines are used; EPO applies the problem‑solution approach for inventive step (Appendix A13.08.1). The Guidelines state which Articles/Rules provide authority and how EP practice is applied mutatis mutandis when ISPE is silent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject‑matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of subject‑matter to be excluded from search/examination, referencing Art.17(2)(a)(i), Rule 39 and Art.34(4)(a)(i), Rule 67.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO has selected specific policy options from the ISPE Guidelines (Appendix to Chapter 9, Point A9.07: Option [2] applies). Computer programs and other potentially excluded matter are handled according to the EPO's chosen options (see Appendix to Chapter 9, Point A9.15: Programs for computers Option [2] applies). Exclusion decisions and cross‑references to EP practice are provided in the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention is treated under Rule 13 and covered in Parts F and in Part B (search matters) and Part C (procedural aspects in Chapter II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes procedures for finding lack of unity at search and examination stages, issuing invitations to pay additional search/examination fees, handling additional search fees and protests (forms PCT/ISA/206, PCT/IPEA/405), and the review procedure (review fee, Form PCT/SISA/503, PCT/ISA/212, PCT/IPEA/420).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficiency of disclosure is governed by Art.5 and is dealt with in Part F (The International Application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must check that the application discloses the invention sufficiently for the skilled person; sequence listing handling and late furnishing impacts search and examination (see B‑VIII and references). Where EPO and ISPE guidance overlap, EP Guidelines are applied mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and formal requirements of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of claims and other formal requirements are governed by Art.6 and related formal requirements, addressed in Part F, Chapter IV (Claims (Art. 6 and formal requirements)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains examples concerning essential features and guidance on claim drafting/interpretation; where ISPE is silent EPO/EP practice on interpretation (including options chosen in Annex II) is applied. Multiple dependent claims, interpretation and conciseness follow the EPO‑selected ISPE options (see Appendix to Chapter 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to priority and priority document handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Right to priority is governed by Art.8 and related Rules; the Guidelines set out requirements for priority claims and handling of priority documents (including fee for certified copy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing parts/elements are later furnished, the 'completely contained' test (Rule 20.6) determines whether the original filing date is preserved. The test for 'completely contained' is stricter than the added‑subject‑matter test and requires identity (or translation) with the priority document; examiner checks and reporting obligations (WO‑ISA/IPER) are specified. The fee and time limits for restoration of priority rights are set out (fee to be paid within two months from expiry of the priority period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of amendments / added subject‑matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowability of amendments is governed by Art.19(2), Art.34(2)(b) and, for substantive assessment, the EPO applies Art.123(2) EPC guidelines mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must examine all amended pages (description, claims, drawings) to see whether they introduce subject‑matter not originally disclosed; amendments taken into consideration are not automatically allowable. Detailed cross‑references to the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO (sections H‑IV etc.) apply; many examples and rules (intermediate generalisations, disclaimers, broadening, deletion, etc.) are given and should be applied case‑by‑case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of defects and errors (substitute sheets and rectification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for correction of defects and errors are governed by Rule 26 (substitute sheets) and Rule 91 (rectification of obvious mistakes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute sheets (Rule 26) retain the original filing date if submitted within time limits and are stamped 'SUBSTITUTE SHEET (RULE 26)'. Rectification under Rule 91 is authorised only if: (i) the mistake is obvious to the skilled person (something else was intended than what appears) and (ii) the rectification is obvious (nothing else could have been intended). Time limit: request must be filed within 26 months from priority date. If authorised, replacement pages are stamped 'RECTIFIED SHEET (RULE 91.1)'. If refused, reasons must be given and applicant may request the IB to publish the refused request with reasons (subject to fee). Substantive allowability of corrections is assessed by the same criteria as for Rule 139 EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing format and timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings forming part of the description must meet Annex C to the Administrative Instructions under the PCT when filed in text format; late furnishing has specific fees and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sequence listings are filed in text format and application is filed electronically, pages of the sequence listing are excluded from the page fee calculation; other filing formats count pages. Late furnishing of sequence listings attracts a fee payable within one month of invitation, and late furnishing affects the WO‑ISA and subsequent examination (see GL/PCT‑EPO B‑VIII, B‑XI, C‑VIII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: types, amounts, methods of payment and currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for payment of fees, expenses and prices (transmittal fee, international filing fee, international search fee, additional fees, fees to IPEA, IB, etc.), methods of payment and currency (all fees to EPO must be paid in euros).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Latest amounts published on EPO and WIPO websites and in Official Journals. Fees payable within month of receipt of application (specifics per fee). Payment methods: bank transfer, debiting deposit account (automatic/individual debit orders filed via accepted electronic means or mandatory forms), cheque abolished, credit cards not accepted. Date of payment established per EPO Rules relating to Fees. Detailed list of fee types and who collects them (RO/EP, ISA/EP, IB, IPEA/EP) provided; reductions and refunds rules in Part A‑II sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: International filing fee structure and page fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: International filing fee consists of a fixed basic amount and an additional 'page fee' for each sheet above 30 (including abstract even if missing at filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must compute and pay additional page fees within one month of receipt; failure to do so can only be remedied with a late payment fee after invitation. Sequence listing pages may be excluded from page count if filed electronically in the required text format (Annex C). Guidance on reductions also provided (electronic filing reductions: web‑form, PDF, XML).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late payment fee and withdrawal consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If required fees are unpaid or insufficient, the RO/EP invites the applicant to pay the missing amount together with a late payment fee; if not paid within one month of invitation the international application is considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late payment fee equals 50% of the unpaid fee or, if that would be less than the transmittal fee, equal to the transmittal fee; it may not exceed 50% of the international filing fee (without page fees). Payment made before issuance of the invitation is considered on time. If payment is made after issuance but before notification of withdrawal is dispatched, payment is considered in time and application not withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional search/examination fees, protests and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for handling findings of lack of unity: invitation to pay additional search/exam fees (Forms PCT/ISA/206, PCT/IPEA/405), payment of additional fees, protest fees, and review fees for supplementary searches or protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional search/exam fees are payable within one month of invitation. Protest fee is payable to have a finding reviewed; review fee applies to SISA processes. Forms, time limits and amounts fixed by EPO; review outcomes communicated by specified forms (PCT/ISA/212, PCT/IPEA/420, PCT/SISA/503).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for 'completely contained' when adding missing parts from priority document
rubrics_metrics.description: If missing parts/elements are furnished after filing, Rule 20.6 allows restoration of the original filing date only if the missing material was 'completely contained' in the priority document (identity or translation required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'completely contained' test is stricter than the added‑subject‑matter test. If EPO is the RO examiner checks for additional technical content; if EPO is not the RO, examiner must check identity of drawings and word‑for‑word identity of text where available. If not completely contained, the filing date is the date on which parts were furnished; examiner should indicate doubts in WO‑ISA/IPER and include relevant documents for re‑dating scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to drawings and title
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to drawings are generally restricted (Art.34(2)(b)); title is part of the description and may be composed or amended by the search examiner if absent or non‑complying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New drawings normally cannot be added because they are not unambiguously derivable from the text; amendments to drawings must be carefully checked for compliance with Art.34(2)(b). Under Rule 37.2 and Rule 5.1 the search examiner may compose/amend the title; before IPEA the title can be amended like any other part of description under Art.34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimers (undisclosed and disclosed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of disclaimers follows the Guidelines in the EPO practice; undisclosed disclaimers are addressed under the EPO's selected ISPE option A20.21[2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should apply the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO mutatis mutandis when assessing disclaimers not disclosed in the application as originally filed versus disclaimers that are disclosed. Specific EPO option choices (Appendix to Chapter 20) are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes – substantive test and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectification under Rule 91 can be requested for obvious mistakes in application documents (description, claims, drawings, abstract, and request form where RO competence applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two cumulative criteria: (i) the mistake must be obvious to the skilled person that something else was intended; (ii) the rectification must be obvious such that nothing else could have been intended. Time limit: 26 months from priority date. Examiner must check timeliness and criteria; authorisation is indicated in WO‑ISA/WO‑IPEA/IPER; partial authorisations indicate which corrections are allowable and which are not, with reasons for refusals. Authorised replacements are stamped accordingly; applicant may request publication of refused request within two months (fee applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between PCT‑EPO Guidelines, ISPE Guidelines and EP Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT‑EPO Guidelines are complementary to, but not a substitute for, the ISPE and RO Guidelines and the PCT Applicant's Guide; where ISPE is silent EPO applies EP Guidelines mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross‑references to EP Guidelines are used when practice is the same; when practices partially overlap the PCT‑EPO Guidelines contain full information. Annex I provides an EPC‑PCT equivalence table; Annex II lists EPO choices where ISPE gives alternative options. The Guidelines do not constitute legal provisions but indicate expected EPO practice in normal occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO choices of ISPE policy options (Annex II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ISPE Guidelines leave ISAs/IPEAs a choice between alternative guidelines, the EPO has selected specific options for use as ISA/IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex II lists chosen options, e.g.: Appendix to Chapter 4 Point A4.05 References to prior art Option [1]; Appendix to Chapter 5 multiple dependent claims Option [2]; interpretation of claims Option [2]; 'use' claims first sentence applied; product‑by‑process Option [1]; conciseness Option [2]; Appendix to Chapter 9 excluded subject matter Option [2]; programs for computers Option [2]; Appendix to Chapter 12 novelty effective date Option [1]; Appendix to Chapter 13 EPO applies problem‑solution approach; Appendix to Chapter 14 industrial applicability criterion applied; Appendix to Chapter 20 disclaimer Option [2]. Examiners must apply these EPO choices when acting as ISA/IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and official communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific PCT/EPO forms are prescribed for search, written opinions, protests, supplementary search requests, partial search reports, invitations to pay additional fees, notifications of decisions on protests, communications from IPEA, WO‑ISA and WO‑IPEA (e.g., PCT/ISA/210, PCT/ISA/237, PCT/ISA/206, PCT/IPEA/405, PCT/IPEA/409, PCT/IPEA/428, PCT/SISA/501, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms must be used where mandatory (e.g., debit orders on certain forms), and the Guidelines list which form applies to each communication. Forms can be found on WIPO's website. Where a particular form is referenced in a procedure, the time limits, fees and consequences tied to that form apply as set out in the Guidelines.
